T.G. Shivashankare Gowda, J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

In this appeal, the appellants have challenged the judgment dated 15.06.2018 passed in M.V.C.No.695 of 2016 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Chincholi (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal' for short).
2. The parties will be referred with respect to their status before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
3. Briefly stated the facts are that, petitioners are the parents of Kiran, the deceased.

The deceased met with a road accident that took place on 25.12.2015, the Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-39/K-5936 in which he was pillion, was capsized on the road near the land of one Rathnamma on Bhadlapur-Devagiri road ridden by one Kiran Reddy.
The deceased died at Pinsiya Meridian Hospital, Hyderabad on 28-12-2015.
Petitioners claimed compensation of Rs.30,90,000/-.

They pleaded that deceased was aged 16 years, student and doing part time job earning Rs.9,000/-
per month.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company, so also its liability.
The Tribunal awarded Rs.7,86,100/- with 6% interest and fastened the liability against the owner of the motor cycle.

4. The petitioners are before this court pleading inadequacy of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, that income taken is on the lower side, so also the amount awarded under conventional heads and fastening liability against the owner of the motor cycle instead of Insurance Company.

5. Heard the arguments of Sri.Harshavardhana R Malipatil, learned counsel for the petitioners and Smt.Anuradha M. Desai, learned counsel for respondent No.2/Insurance Company.
Saraswati And Anr vs Ashok Reddy And Anr on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29134158/
2 6.

entities.text: Saraswati And Anr vs Ashok Reddy And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: According to the learned counsel for petitioners, the deceased, though a student, was doing part time job, earning Rs.9,000/- per month, compensation under conventional heads though settled, it was awarded on the lower side and he sought for re-assessment and enhancement and to fasten the liability against the Insurance Company.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for Insurance Company contended that the Tribunal has correctly assessed the income of the deceased as he was not an earner being student, the compensation under conventional heads may be assessed, as settled in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others -2017 ACJ 680.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others -2017 ACJ 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is also contended that, the rider of the motor cycle was a minor,
he has no right to hold any Driving Licence, there is no liability on the part of the Insurance Company, Tribunal has rightly noted it and fastened the liability against the owner and supported the impugned judgment.
8.
We have given our anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the parties and perused the records.
9. As we notice, the Tribunal has considered the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month.

Having regard to the evidence that the deceased was also doing part time job being a student, the income so assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side and it ought to have considered minimum of Rs.8,000/- per month for a person who has no proof of income, taking into consideration the accident was of the year 2015.
Hence, we assess the income of the deceased accordingly.
10. As seen from the impugned judgment, the Tribunal has not considered the future prospects and also the conventional heads.

By applying the principles laid down in Pranay Sethi's case (supra),
future prospects should be taken as 40% for age below 40 years for a person who has no permanent job, so also compensation under conventional head has already been settled.
Ex.P5/Postmortem report confirms that the deceased was aged 16 years.

Hence, applicable multiplier as per decision of Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation (2009)6 SCC 121, is '18'.
11.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation (2009)6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
If all these factors are taken into consideration the assessment of loss of dependency would be:
Rs.8,000/- (Income of the deceased) + Rs.3,200/- (40% future prospects) =
Rs.11,200/- per month.
The petitioners are the parents of the deceased and the deceased was a bachelor, 50% has to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased.
It comes to Rs.5,600/- per month and Rs.67,200/- per year multiplied by '18', it comes to Rs.12,09,600/-.
Under the conventional heads, each of the petitioners is entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards loss of love and affection, towards loss of estate and funeral expenses Rs.15,000/- each.
The deceased died during the treatment, for which the petitioners have spent a sum of Rs.23,100/- and that amount needs to be reimbursed.

The total compensation comes to Rs.12,09,600/- +
Rs.1,10,000/- + Rs.23,100/- = Rs.13,42,700/- as against Rs.7,86,100/- awarded by the Tribunal, an enhancement of Rs.5,56,600/-.
It is the just compensation to which the petitioners are entitled in the facts and circumstances of the case.

3 12.

entities.text: Saraswati And Anr vs Ashok Reddy And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Another grievance of the petitioners is that, the liability is fastened against the owner of the motor cycle.
Before the Tribunal, the petitioners have relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Singh Ram -vs- Nirmala and Others - (2018) 3 SCC 800.

entities.text: Singh Ram -vs- Nirmala and Others - (2018) 3 SCC 800
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal though referred to the said judgment offered an explanation that the direction issued by the Hon'ble Apex Court to the Insurance Company to pay and then recover, was by invoking the extra-ordinary jurisdiction which the Tribunal do not have.

As we notice at para-20 of the impugned judgment, the Tribunal is very categorical that the owner of the motor cycle has violated the conditions of the insurance policy and for this reason, the owner has to pay the compensation.

In Singh Ram's case (supra), the Hon'ble Apex Court while dealing with the owner, who placed fake driving licence and later a lapsed driving licence renewed after its expiry, referring to the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Swaran Singh - (2004) 3 SCC 297 directed the Insurance Company to pay and recover the compensation amount.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Swaran Singh - (2004) 3 SCC 297
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. In Jawahar Singh -vs- Bala Jain and Others - (2011) 6 SCC 425, the Hon'ble Apex Court referring to a minor causing the accident, who had no licence to ride the motor cycle, directed the Insurance Company to pay the compensation and to recover it from the owner.

entities.text: Jawahar Singh -vs- Bala Jain and Others - (2011) 6 SCC 425
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. Learned counsel for the petitioners have relied upon the judgment in Pappu and Others -vs- Vinod Kumar Lamba and Another - (2018) 3 SCC 208 to submit that the Hon'ble Apex Court applied the principle of 'pay and recovery' in case of violation of policy conditions.

entities.text: Pappu and Others -vs- Vinod Kumar Lamba and Another - (2018) 3 SCC 208
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that these are the principles applicable in case of any violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.
We are not in agreement with the said arguments, as the Tribunal has categorically recorded that there is violation of terms of the policy.
Admittedly, the motor cycle was ridden by a minor aged 17 years, who had no capacity to hold the Driving Licence.
Even under such circumstances, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the judgments referred supra directed the application of principle of 'pay and recovery'.
Hence, the Tribunal has committed an error in directing the owner to pay the compensation.
The Tribunal ought to have directed the Insurance Company to pay the compensation and to - 10 - recover it from the owner.
Hence, the impugned order needs modification accordingly.
16. In view of the above discussions, the appeal deserves to be allowed.

In the result, we pass the following:
ORDER
The appeal is allowed in part.
The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.
